description: A pinned input for independent evidence consumers of aps:action-result:v1. Each case keeps four sources of expectation apart: what the published draft-03 text says, what the pinned TypeScript SDK returns on two separate surfaces, what the pinned Python SDK returns and which surface it does not implement, and what Agent Replay's stated binding rules imply for the record. Nothing here merges those into a single verdict, and a case may be stage-valid and composite-invalid at the same time.

blocks.draft03: The expectation derived from the published draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 text, with the section and line. Authored from the text, not from any implementation.
blocks.sdk_ts: What agent-passport-system 7.0.0 actually returns, recorded from real runs, on two separate entrypoints: validateReceiptStageV1 (section 5.3 stage rules for one record) and verifyReceiptWithDecisionV1 (the section 5.6 composite check against supplied decision evidence).
blocks.sdk_py: What agent-passport-system 4.0.0 for Python actually returns from validate_receipt_stage_v1, recorded from real runs, plus an explicit statement that the pinned release has no counterpart to verifyReceiptWithDecisionV1.
blocks.replay_policy: What Agent Replay's binding rules, as stated by its author, imply for this record. Derived by this suite by applying those stated rules to the record. Agent Replay was not run here, these records were not submitted to it, and no outcome in this block was reported for them. Where the stated rules do not settle a record, the block says unresolved_until_run rather than guessing.

replay_policy_stated_rules.source: stated by the Agent Replay author at revision 08b3146097977db565a202c7a8f34d350da00fd0 in Agent-Authority-Conformance/aps-conformance-suite#99
full_binding_requires: matching decision_ref when the decision carries one
replay_policy_stated_rules.partially_bound: missing actor, wrong prev, or wrong decision_ref leaves the result only partially bound
replay_policy_stated_rules.not_stated: The stated rules say nothing about an actor that is present but mismatched, and nothing about a record that fails the APS schema before any binding rule is reached.

classifications.aps_conformance: The SDK outcome matches the draft-03 expectation. Where Python cannot exercise the surface the case turns on, the case stays aps_conformance and sdk_py is marked not_implemented.
classifications.draft03_stated_relation_not_enforced: Draft-03 states a relation between two members and lists the check among the verifier steps, without a BCP 14 keyword on either statement. The current reference SDKs do not enforce that relation. This is neither a lab pass nor a normative conformance failure.
classifications.draft03_semantic_relation_not_explicitly: Two draft-03 definitions describe the same role, the record makes them disagree, and the draft states no explicit equality relation and names no verifier step that compares them. Not an APS violation, not an APS negative vector, and not Replay-only.

chain_receipts.note: The three chain receipts, exercised by both runners on the same three surfaces: receipt_id recomputed from the record, every boundary signature verified over the section 5.2 signature payload, and the section 5.3 stage rules applied. Recorded from real runs of agent-passport-system 7.0.0 and 4.0.0 for Python, which agree on all three.

draft03.statement: The record is the action-result stage section 5.3.3 describes: issuer is the enforcement boundary, prev is the consumed policy-decision receipt_id, decision_ref equals that decision's decision_ref, and result carries exactly profile, status, effect_ref and error_code with status succeeded and a non-null effect_ref. The decision it follows carries a valid_until later than its own issued_at.

decision_ref_binding.note: Which decision this case was checked against, pinned so the composite result above cannot be reproduced with the other decision's evidence substituted. The digest is buildDecisionRefV1 over decision_evidence.permit and this record's own action_ref, which is the value verifyReceiptWithDecisionV1 compares with record.decision_ref.

replay_policy.rule: All four conditions the stated rules give for full binding hold: action_ref matches the decision's, subject_agent is present and matches, prev equals the consumed decision's receipt_id, and decision_ref matches the decision the chain names.

draft03.statement: subject_agent is a REQUIRED member of the closed ReceiptV1 object. It appears in the envelope at line 962 and is defined at line 981 as the acting agent; lines 984-988 name decision_ref and prev as the only conditional members, and lines 988-989 say a member that is not applicable is absent, not null. subject_agent is always applicable, so its absence is a structural failure, which section 5.6 line 1225 makes invalid.

This record is not a valid ReceiptV1: subject_agent is a REQUIRED member and it is absent, so the record fails the APS schema before any binding rule is known to apply. The stated rules say nothing about that case, so this suite does not assign one.

draft03.statement: Section 5.3.3 lines 1104-1105 say prev is the consumed policy-decision receipt_id. This record names the action-intent receipt_id instead. Section 5.6 line 1219 lists validate prev and stage transitions among the verifier steps, so the relation is named on the verifier side as well as the producer side. Neither statement carries a BCP 14 keyword, which section 1.1 lines 175-179 confine to words that appear in all capitals; the MUST in the same sentence at line 1105 governs decision_ref, not prev.

cases.classification_note: Draft-03 states the prev relation at section 5.3.3 lines 1104-1105 and lists prev validation among the section 5.6 verifier steps at line 1219. Neither statement carries a BCP 14 keyword. Neither reference SDK resolves prev today: the TypeScript stage validator says so in its own doc comment (src/v2/receipt-core/stage.ts, 'does not resolve prev against the receipt it names') and the Python module docstring says the same ('no resolution of prev against the record it names'). Both therefore accept this record. The stated relation is not enforced by the current reference SDKs. That is neither a lab pass nor a normative conformance failure.

cases.defect: decision_ref set to the decision_ref of a second policy-decision minted for the same intent with verdict deny, so the value is a well-formed real digest; receipt_id recomputed and the boundary signature redone over the mutated body

draft03.statement: Section 5.3.3 lines 1105-1106 say decision_ref MUST equal that decision's decision_ref, where that decision is the consumed policy-decision named by prev. This record's prev still names the permit decision while its decision_ref names the deny decision, so the two disagree. Section 5.6 line 1218 has a verifier recompute decision_ref where required.

cases.defect: action_ref set to the action_ref of a different fixed action that keeps the same agent_id, the same action_type and the same scope_required and changes only the target, decision_ref left unchanged; receipt_id recomputed and the boundary signature redone over the mutated body

draft03.statement: Decision binding fails. decision_ref is computed over a closed DecisionRefV1 input whose members are profile, action_ref, authority_state_ref, policy_ref, context_ref and decision_output_ref, in that order; profile is the first member at line 1158 and action_ref the second at line 1159. Lines 1093-1094 say a permit or narrow policy-decision record is a bounded, single-use approval for its action_ref. This record carries the decision_ref of a decision made over the primary action while naming a different action_ref, so the reference cannot be recomputed from the decision the boundary made. Section 5.6 lines 1216-1218 have a verifier recompute action_ref from the independently supplied action and recompute decision_ref where required.

draft03.statement: aps-action-ref-v2 commits to agent_id, which draft-03 defines as the acting agent's identifier (4.1, line 789), and ReceiptV1 defines subject_agent as the acting agent (5.1, line 981). action_ref is unchanged in this case, so the record names two different acting agents. Draft-03 states no explicit equality relation between subject_agent and the action_ref agent_id, and section 5.6 lines 1213-1221 name no verifier comparison between them.
